subject: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Jordan - thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + recommended next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive:

Summary of needs (as I heard it)
- End-user search + contextual Q&A over your product docs + support KB (high freshness, medium latency requirement)
- Need high grounding / low hallucination for regulatory content (billing + legal)
- Target throughput: ~200 qps at peak; expect bursty traffic from support flows

Redwood recommendations (initial)
- Candidate model(s): rwd-13b-q4_0 (good balance of latency / grounding when paired with a strong retriever), fallback: Llama-3-13B-8k for higher-quality long-form responses
- Embeddings: rwd-embed-3 (512 dim) for vector index consistency across retrievers
- Retriever config: HNSW index, ef_search=128, recall k=10; document chunking 500 tokens with overlap 50
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker (rwd-rerank-large) at top-10 to improve precision@k; bi-encoder for low-cost pre-filtering
- Grounding metrics to track: grounding_precision@k, hallucination_rate (manual sampling + automated similarity cutoff), grounding_coverage (percent of answers with at least one grounded result)

Attachments & links included:
- ACME_RAG_prompt_sets_v1.xlsx (prompt templates + eval prompts)
- redwood_rag_benchmarks_202608.pdf (end-to-end latency / grounding benchmarks on similar datasets)
- Shared drive with detailed eval harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedDrive

Immediate next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Lukas (SE) - 60m to review retrieval architecture, sample dataset access, and run a quick smoke benchmark (Lukas to propose times)
2) Grant us read-only access to a representative dataset (subset of docs + support transcripts) - we recommend 5k docs to start
3) Redwood will run a smoke eval (benchmarks + prompt set) and return a cleanup plan + cost/throughput estimates within 5 business days of dataset access

I'm copying Lukas and Michael to coordinate the technical deep-dive. If this captures things correctly, I'll send a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a calendar invite.

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Jordan - great questions. Short answers here, and we'll cover the rest in the deep-dive:

Quantization & fidelity
- rwd-13b-q4_0 is Q4 quantized and tuned for inference throughput; in our internal benchmarks it matches or slightly trails Llama-3-13B on open-ended quality, but when paired with a cross-encoder reranker+strong retriever it achieves comparable grounding metrics at lower latency/cost. We'll include the head-to-head numbers in the smoke eval report.

End-to-end artifacts
- We'll deliver a smoke benchmark pack: latency P95/P99, tokens per second, grounding precision@k, hallucination sampling with examples, and cost estimate per 1M queries. Expect that within 5 business days of dataset access.

MAP + timeline
- I'll send a 1-page MAP by EOD that covers dataset access, roles, deliverables, and acceptance criteria for the PoC. Tentative timeline: dataset onboarding (1-2 days), smoke run (2-3 days), report & recommendations (1 day).

Action: I'm sending a Doodle and some times for the deep-dive now. Lukas - can you scope an initial smoke plan (what we'll run, minimal infra) so Jordan/procurement can see the cost outline?

Thanks -
Marissa

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Jordan / team - quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive with some concrete defaults we'll start with and the grounding metrics to instrument. Happy to adjust based on your infra.

Default smoke config (recommended)
- Retriever: Faiss HNSW (index on 512-d rwd-embed-3 vectors), ef_search=128, ef_construction=200, M=32
- k for retrieval: 10 (we'll evaluate sensitivity at k=5/20)
- Chunking: 500-token chunks, 50-token overlap; keep original doc ids for traceability
- Reranker: rwd-rerank-large cross-encoder applied to top-10; thresholding: rerank_score >= 0.70 to declare "grounded"
- Answer assembly: strict grounding first (concatenate top grounded chunks up to 1024 tokens), then generation with rwd-13b-q4_0; fallback to Llama-3-13B for low-confidence long-form responses

Metrics & validation plan
- Grounding precision@k (precision of top answer when at least one ranked chunk >= threshold)
- Hallucination sampling: random sample of 100 answers evaluated by SME against source text
- Grounding coverage: % queries with at least one chunk above reranker threshold
- Latency (P50/P95/P99) end-to-end and per-stage (retrieval, rerank, generation)
- Cost per 1k queries (projected) using our conservative usage model

Deliverables for smoke run (what you'll get)
- End-to-end report with per-metric charts + example failure cases
- Prompt-set file (we'll tune prompts in prompt_sets_v1)
- Recommended production config and an estimate for Dedicated capacity if you want predictable throughput

Link to the eval harness + starter metrics dashboard: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedDrive (I've dropped a sample config under /acme/poc/config.yaml)

If you can grant read-only access to a 5k-doc subset and a sample of 2k support transcripts, I can run the smoke run within 48-72 hours.

--
